mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) has a negative relationship with S&P 500 20-day forward returns, meaning that lower rates predict higher returns. This relationship is active at all times, so the signal is always active without requiring a threshold condition.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 2.0% signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns due to increased risk aversion and reduced liquidity. The signal is activated when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.0%.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns in periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 0.5% and the unemployment rate exceeds 5.5%, it signals a recessionary environment with high policy support but weak labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns. This interaction between monetary policy and labor market conditions is the active signal.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% AND UNRATE > 5.5% are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A housing market recovery (HOUST > 1200) signals strong economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to improved corporate earnings outlook. The signal is active only when housing starts exceed 1200.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods when HOUST > 1200 are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 5.5%) signals a weak labor market and potential recession, leading to negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns due to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings. The signal is activated when unemployment exceeds 5.5%.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods when UNRATE > 5.5% are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) has a positive relationship with S&P 500 5-day forward returns, meaning that higher production levels predict higher returns. This relationship is active at all times, so the signal is always active without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns in periods when INDPRO is above its 3-month moving average are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When residential fixed investment (RSAFS) exceeds 400,000 and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 250, it signals a strong economy with moderate inflation, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns. This interaction between demand (RSAFS) and monetary (CPIAUCSL) conditions is the active signal.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods when RSAFS > 400000 AND CPIAUCSL > 250 are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI index above 255.0 signals moderate inflation, which is associated with a strong economy and positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns. The signal is activated when CPIAUCSL exceeds 255.0.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods when CPIAUCSL > 255.0 are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
